data.name: Ayeera
data.gender_notes: Ayeera is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Ayeera is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ayu' meaning 'life' and 'Ri' meaning 'night'. The name symbolizes the light of the moon illuminating life during the night. In Hindu mythology, the moon god is often depicted as the giver of life and the sustainer of all beings. The name Ayeera carries the meaning “Moonlight” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayeera usually hope their child will grow to embody moonlight and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayeera total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Ayeera was a 13th century queen of the Chola Dynasty in southern India. She is known for her military prowess and is said to have led several successful battles against invading armies.

Ayeera is also mentioned in the Hindu epic Mahabharata as the daughter of King Dhritarashtra and the sister of Duryodhana. She is described as a virtuous and beautiful princess who married the Pandava prince Bhima.
